narrative:
Your application was denied because the model predicted a 51% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt, meaning the risk was slightly higher than the threshold for acceptance. This was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward failure, as it suggests a steep decline in your later academic performance that raised concerns about your readiness for the exam.

Your family income being lower-middle class, compared to the majority of successful students who come from upper-middle or middle-class backgrounds, may have indirectly influenced your academic journey, but it was not a direct factor in the model’s decision. Additionally, your part-time enrollment status, which is rare among successful students (only 6.8% were part-time), could have affected your ability to focus on studies, though it was not among the top three factors.

To improve your chances in the future, focus on strengthening your academic performance in your final years of school, as this was the most critical factor. Consider retaking the LSAT to boost your score closer to the average of successful students, and explore full-time enrollment if possible to align with the profile of typical bar exam passers.
